thread:
alex: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: what exactly is the new release rhythm? i heard something about 3-week windows?
maya: TL;DR: moving to a 3-week minor release cycle + a hard monthly major release (security + schema bumps). intent is more predictable windows for teams + customers.
chris: Are there blackout windows for Dedicated customers or maintenance windows we need to communicate?
founder-cto: We keep the current emergency blackout policy (no non-critical deploys during major customer maintenance windows). Normal minor releases should avoid major holidays; ops will publish a calendar.
alex: Feature flags: do we still require them for all customer-impacting changes?
maya: Yes. Anything that changes user-visible behavior must be feature flagged or rolled out as a controlled canary for at least 24 hours. Exceptions: pure infra fixes with no API change.
chris: Canary question: recommended traffic % and monitoring checklist?
ops: Recommend start at 5-10% for 4 hours, then 25% for 12 hours before full ramp. Must monitor error-rate, latency p95/p99, and synthetic checks. If any of these exceed thresholds (error-rate >0.5% absolute or latency p99 >15% above baseline), rollback.
oncall-bot: Reminder: file a canary runbook in the release ticket and ping @ops 24h before canary start.
maya: On quality bars: unit + integration passing is required, plus a blue-green e2e smoke run in staging. Also need perf profile: no p99 regressions >15% vs release baseline and p95 within 10%.
alex: Who owns the rollback/runbook? Is it the eng lead or SRE?
chris: Eng lead owns the rollout plan, SRE/ops owns the runbook template and monitors. Both are expected to be in the roll call for critical ramps.
sam: SLA impacts: any change to hosted API SLAs with this cadence? customers are asking during renewals.
founder-cto: No SLA changes for hosted. We will, however, surface per-customer and per-route SLO dashboards internally so account teams can see risk trends before renewals.
alex: Post-release: can we add a lightweight retro? 10-15m to capture regressions and lessons learned.
ops: Strong +1. Recommend a 15m blameless sync within 24h for any release that hits rollback or triggered alerts. For regular releases a 10m async notes template is fine.
docs: I can draft a short "release checklist" doc that includes cadence, canary template, notification matrix, and rollback triggers. Want volunteers to review.
maya: I'll pair with docs. Also will open a PR to the handbook to codify the calendar and the oncall notify flow by next Wednesday.
chris: Any changes to oncall rotation or handover expectations?
ops: No rotation frequency changes. Handover notes must include active rollouts and pending canaries. If you plan a canary crossing oncall shifts, confirm with the incoming oncall 12h before.
oncall-bot: Auto-note: deployment notification channels should include #incidents, + direct mention of the oncall alias.
alex: Example commands for the deploy tooling?
chris: Use the deploy CLI: `deployctl release --svc inference-api --canary 8 --monitor 12h --notify ops`
sam: Can we get a short customer-facing blurb we can share when asked about stability and cadence?
founder-cto: Yes. Docs + comms will produce a one-pager: "Our release cadence and reliability commitments". Internal draft linked here once ready.
alex: thanks all. once the PR and the docs draft are up please tag the renewal & sales reps so they can use the blurb. :thumbsup:
